thread:
maria: Thinking out loud — what if we prototyped an "auctioneer" style allocator for continuous batching? idea: tenants post short-lived bids (priority, max-latency, token-value) and the scheduler runs a fast market-clearing loop to assemble batches that maximize economic value while respecting latency budgets.
kevin: Ooh. Like a tiny in-memory market every 10ms? love the thought but worried about jitter and OS scheduling noise.
nate: Could help with utilization vs SLOs tradeoff. We already have per-tenant headroom signals; this could slot into that as a scoring function instead of fixed credits.
alice: Curious about overhead. market loop + matching adds CPU cycles each scheduling tick. how do we avoid adding more latency than we save?
maria: Right — target is microsecond-scale matching. sketch: keep bids as lightweight structs, pre-bucketed by latency class, run a single-threaded matching loop on the batching core. fallback to FIFO if match time exceeds threshold.
carol: And caching interactions? packs that win the auction might be small and cause more KV cache thrash. need affinity hints in bids (warm/Cold) so matching coalesces similar prefixes.
kevin: Also need preemption semantics. If a high-value bid arrives, can we evict a queued lower-value batch before it locks kernels? eviction should only reclaim queue slots, not in-progress GPU work.
maria: Exactly — design constraint: only preempt waiting groups, never running groups. kernel-granularity preemption remains out of scope.
infra-bot: deploy-batcher-proto deployed to staging at 2025-09-03T14:02:00Z :rocket:
nate: For scoring function, propose simple utility = value_per_token * expected_tokens - latency_penalty. latency_penalty = alpha * max(0, expected_latency - SLO). alpha tunable by tenant tier.
alice: We'll need good estimates for expected_tokens and expected_latency. can we piggyback on recent-per-tenant histograms? that should be cheap.
carol: Yep. Also add a stability term to avoid oscillation: penality for displacing same-tenant groups repeatedly. think of a small hysteresis.
kevin: Experiment plan: implement matching loop + scoring in a new opt-in scheduler variant. Run A/B on a single-pool GPU fleet with synthetic mixes: latency-sensitive (short, high-priority) + background batch (long, cheap). measure p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU occupancy, and token-cost.
maria: If occupancy improves without p99 regressions, we iterate. fallback: if regressions seen, fall back to current credit-based allocator per-tenant.
nate: Edge cases: bursty tenants posting many tiny high-value bids could starve medium-priority tenants. propose per-tenant rate limit on outstanding bids + a fairness floor in the objective.
alice: Implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
struct Bid { tenant_id, value_per_token, expected_tokens, max_latency_ms, affinity_hint };
loop every 10ms {
  collect bids;
  bucket by latency class;
  greedy match to fill target batch size maximizing utility with fairness floor;
  dispatch batches to GPU queue;
}
```
carol: Nice. Ops thoughts: observability must show bid churn, match latency, and how much utility each batch captured. add a small telemetry surface ASAP.
kevin: Rollout concerns: start with low-risk tenants (internal + beta customers) and allow an override header to force FIFO. Also expose a safety toggle: if match-loop latency > 2ms, switch to safe allocator.
maria: Next steps: nate + alice pair on prototype for 2 weeks, carol add cache-affinity hints, kevin wire canary flags. I'll draft a short RFC appendix describing objective and safety invariants.
alice: ack, will spin up a microbench harness and generate synthetic bidder behavior.
nate: I'll add the fairness floor math and a sim harness to test adversarial bidders.
carol: I'll draft the telemetry dashboard fields.
kevin: +1, excited to see if a small market can give us better packing without hurting SLOs. :eyes:
